description: Italian vocabulary register audit list. 'formal' = written-prose/bureaucratic item dead in conversation; 'preferred' = what Italian speakers actually say. Deck defaults: tu/Lei address, passato prossimo in dialogue. Severity: 'high' = dead in speech, swap wherever it appears in conversational cards; 'medium' = written-leaning, swap in beginner content. See docs/italian-register-policy.md.

dead_in_speech.rationale: Written-Italian pronouns, determiners, and connectors that no Italian uses in conversation.

entries.note: Subject pronouns of formal writing only. Spoken Italian uses lui/lei/loro or drops the pronoun.
Bureaucratic and old-Tuscan demonstrative; survives only in officialese («codesto ufficio») and irony.
«recarsi presso l'ufficio» is announcement/form language; conversation says andare.
'Aforementioned' — document language; jocular use in speech is intentional register play.
Only as bare relative («l'uomo il quale parla» → «l'uomo che parla»). After prepositions (con il quale, del quale) it is standard — exempt, though con cui is lighter.
